name: The Life You Can Save (Founders Pledge)
summary: Raises money for effective global poverty charities by promoting effective giving. Founders Pledge's page gives a gross multiplier of about 17 dollars raised per dollar received; our view takes today's ratio (9.19, 2025), counts a marginal dollar at half the average (by default; a value you set) and values each dollar moved by the site's shared method: half of it new money, the rest credited for the gain over GiveDirectly, going to the charities The Life You Can Save's own 2025 split names, each at its live result.

sections.title: Founders Pledge's figure
sections.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figures, as its recommendation page states them. It publishes no spreadsheet for this recommendation, so these are the model's only evaluator rows.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Money moved today
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's: Founders Pledge's multiplier was for 2019–2021, and a donation today buys today's ratio. Each dollar moved is then valued by the site's shared method (docs/normalization.md 2.8).

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Dollars raised for high-impact charities per dollar received (gross)

source.title: Founders Pledge, The Life You Can Save (recommendation page)
source.quote: We estimate that in 2021 they raised $17 dollars for high-impact charities for every dollar they received.

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's figure, quoted on its page; The Life You Can Save reports its 17:1 as a three-year ratio for 2019–2021, and Founders Pledge expects "a gross multiplier of ~17x over the next few years". Gross: it doesn't remove money donors would have given anyway.

rows.label: Gross multiplier in recent years, as a share of Founders Pledge's 17

source.title: The Life You Can Save, 2025 annual report
source.note: 3-year leverage ratio 9.19:1 (2023–2025: money moved over expenses; $24.07 million moved in 2025 on $2.62 million of expenses). Earlier: 10 (2024 report), 17 (2019–2021).

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge expected about 17 to hold "over the next few years"; The Life You Can Save's own three-year ratio has since fallen to 10 (2024 report) and 9.19 (2025 report, 2023–2025), 54% of 17. A donation today buys today's ratio, so the result uses the latest, 9.19, with Founders Pledge's own 17 (100%) as the high end and 8.5 (50%) as the low end. Founders Pledge's figure stays the model's evaluator row.

rows.label: How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Your value, shared with every model built on an organisation's past average (Your values: "How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far"): the leverage ratio is money moved over all of The Life You Can Save's costs in 2023–2025, an average; the next dollar it receives moves less than the average dollar did. 50% by default (our judgment), from 18% (CEARCH's estimate for Giving What We Can's marginal dollar) to 100% (average = marginal). The evaluator view keeps 100%.

rows.label: Value of a dollar to The Life You Can Save's recommended charities (its 2025 split, live), units of value
rows.explainer: The Life You Can Save's own published split of the money it moved in 2025, by charity, each charity at its main model's live result on this site (GiveDirectly at GiveWell's model, as everywhere in meta models); Evidence Action and Malaria Consortium, which run several programmes, at GiveWell's programme-weighted figure for the charity, as on the rankings (Evidence Action: syphilis screening, iron and folic acid, deworming, in-line chlorination and Dispensers for Safe Water; Malaria Consortium: seasonal malaria chemoprevention over its locations, bed nets and vitamin A). The 19 charities with a model here took $13.4 million of the $24.1 million; the rest (15 charities and its Rapid Response Fund, none modelled here) is valued at the average of these, so it drops out of the mix.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money actually went: its own published split by charity, each at its live result on this site.

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: 1× GiveDirectly), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Shifted money was going to be given anyway; it is credited only for the gain. Where it would have gone is valued at GiveDirectly's live result (GiveWell's model), as Ambitious Impact does, times a shared multiple (1×, from 0 to 3×).

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. Dollars moved per marginal dollar received (Founders Pledge's gross multiplier, at today's ratio, times the share a marginal dollar moves of the average), each worth the site's shared net value of a dollar moved: The Life You Can Save's own 2025 split by charity at their live results, new money in full, shifted money for the gain over GiveDirectly. This model used to keep 40% of the money (our judgment, 20–70%) and value it at 5 times Founders Pledge's cash benchmark (2–10); the shared method replaces both.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for fundraising and outreach organisations: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Marketing and fundraising staff could typically earn more in commercial roles. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Money moved per dollar of The Life You Can Save's cost (marginal)
rows.explainer: Gross money moved by a marginal dollar of cost: what credit by share of resources counts as the donors' contribution (times the new-money share).

rows.label: Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: The site's one formula for every meta charity (src/engine/moved-money.ts): with credit by share of resources on, the donors whose new money the organisation moves are contributors too, alongside staff's forgone pay, so the outcome is shared with them. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: Units of value per dollar, in GiveWell's units (one unit = a year of doubled income for one person). With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
